i.norm:
Tests how the {@code offset} passed to the builder affects the number of readable bytes reported by {@link UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream#available()}.

The expectation is that {@code available()} returns the count of bytes from the requested offset to the end of the buffer, clamped to {@code 0} when the offset reaches or exceeds the buffer length.

Builds a stream over {@code buffer} that starts reading at {@code offset}. The builder only declares a checked exception for origins that need conversion; a plain byte array never does, so any failure is a test bug.
Asserts that a stream over {@code buffer} starting at {@code offset} reports {@code expectedAvailable} readable bytes.
these in-memory streams hold no resources to close
Empty buffer: nothing is ever available, regardless of offset.
Single-byte buffer: one byte available at the start, none once the offset reaches or passes the only element.
Larger buffer: available bytes shrink as the offset moves forward and reach 0 when the offset equals the buffer length.
